key_insight: Predictive triboelectric nanogenerator design requires linking evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay to electrical output across length scales.
engineering_relevance: These links can guide material selection, surface design and circuit integration for mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing.
method: Review polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials against charge retention, compliance and durability requirements.
Assess molecular, contact-mechanical, electrostatic and circuit models by their inputs, predictions and validation evidence.
Organise applications by device scale and propose staged validation of contact mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of model capabilities and experimental validation evidence, not a new quantitative benchmark, and calls for independent testing beyond calibration conditions.
watch_item: Prescribed surface charge density, idealised geometries and nominal contact-area assumptions can limit predictions under realistic loading.
paper_title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
